bull.b: Sustained high gross margins (85% Q1, ~79% TTM) indicate attractive unit economics for the RenovoCath platform. Durable margin advantage supports profitability as procedural volume scales, provides pricing and COGS flexibility, and lowers the incremental cash needed per additional procedure.

Rapid growth in active centers (5→16 in ~18 months) and a 48-center pipeline show durable commercial adoption driven by physician advocacy and repeat orders. A broadening clinical footprint reduces single-center concentration risk and supports recurring device/procedure revenue as centers convert.

bull.t: Very low leverage and stronger equity base
bull.b: Minimal debt burden reduces interest and refinancing risk and preserves financial flexibility. The material equity increase (and recent ~$10M private placement noted in calls) strengthens the balance sheet, giving management runway to pursue commercialization and trial completion without heavy near-term leverage.

bear.b: Consistent ~-$11M annual cash burn is a durable constraint on the business, forcing reliance on external funding unless revenue scales materially. Persistent negative cash flow limits reinvestment capacity, risks dilution from future financings, and could slow manufacturing and commercialization efforts if conversions lag.

bear.t: Modest absolute revenue base and concentration risk
bear.b: While growth rates are strong, the small absolute revenue base means margins and cash flow are fragile: fixed SG&A/R&D costs loom large and quarterly 'chunkiness' from center approvals can cause volatile cash generation. Durable scaling is required to absorb expenses and prove sustainable profitability.

Ongoing listing compliance pressure is a structural governance and capital-access risk. Potential delisting or remediation actions could distract management, reduce liquidity and institutional interest, and complicate future financings or strategic partnerships if unresolved by the deadline.
